name: The Bail Project: policy, public education and research (charityevals' estimate)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: people kept out of pretrial detention by the US state campaigns (Texas, Florida, Oklahoma and others).
summary: The Bail Project's policy, public-education and research work (about $5 million a year with overhead, fiscal 2023-2025) campaigns in the states where it bails people out, and its wins of those years are counted as a past average: a share of the defeat of Texas's 2023 proposals to deny bail more widely (held off two and a half years, until a narrower amendment passed in 2025, plus a tenth of that amendment's effect through the protections it carries) and a share of blocking the 2025 bills against charitable bail in Florida and Oklahoma, each valued as the detention, sentences, lost earnings, jail costs and deaths avoided, with the bail model's shared figures; the campaigns it lost count nothing. The result is about 0.0015 years of healthy life per 1,000 dollars, far below the median of the site's global-health models because the wins are defensive, the charity's share of the coalitions is small and the next dollar counts at 29% of the average, with years of spending in reserve. Both branches are discounted for missing data, and the result is mostly uncertainty: how much detention the defeated measures would have added and how much of their defeat is the campaign's.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

rows.label: Rise in Texas's jail population the 2023 proposals would have caused
rows.explainer: SJR 44 (a constitutional amendment to deny bail for listed violent and repeat felonies) and SB 1318 (more cash bail) failed in 2023 with the charity in the coalition against them. People charged with those offences are already held on high bail, so denial adds mostly the time of those who would have paid: our judgment 1.5% of the jail population (0.3% to 5%), about 1,000 people at a time.

rows.label: Texas: person-years of detention a year the defeated proposals would have added
rows.explainer: People held at any one time is person-years a year.

rows.label: Texas: extra days held per person under denial of bail
rows.explainer: Felony cases take months to close and people denied bail stay until then: 120 days (60 to 240), our judgment.

rows.label: Texas: people a year who would have been held
rows.explainer: Person-years over the days each would have been held.

rows.label: Texas: years until a similar amendment passed anyway
rows.explainer: Texas voters adopted SJR 5, a narrower amendment denying bail for some violent felonies, in November 2025, about two and a half years after the 2023 defeat: the defeat counts those years, as a won reform later repealed counts its years in force.

rows.label: Texas: share of the 2025 amendment's added detention avoided by the protections the coalition won
rows.explainer: The charity 'led a coalition of state and national partners' on SJR 5 (2025 report), which says the amendment as passed 'enshrines critical due process protections' while it lets judges deny bail. Our judgment: those protections avoid a tenth of what it adds (0 to 30%).

rows.label: Texas: years counted, discounted
rows.explainer: The years the defeat held the expansion off, plus the protections' share over the site's years counted for a won reform, after the delay.

rows.label: Texas: share of the defeat due to the opposition campaign
rows.explainer: SJR 44 and SB 1318 died in the 2023 session; such measures fail for many reasons (calendar, other priorities). The defeat is already in, so this is a share of the outcome, not a chance still to be drawn: 30% (10% to 60%), our judgment.

rows.label: Texas: the charity's share of the coalition's resources
rows.explainer: The ACLU of Texas, Texas Civil Rights Project, Texas Appleseed, public defenders and national groups worked against the measures; the charity testified and organised. 10% (3% to 25%), our judgment.

rows.label: Texas: evidence adjustment
rows.explainer: How much detention the proposals would really have added is our own judgment, not a fiscal note: 0.7 (0.4 to 0.9).

rows.label: Texas: missing outcome data
rows.explainer: Thin: the effect of the measures on detention is judged, not measured, so the site's discount for missing data applies.

rows.label: Texas: share of the win delivered
rows.explainer: A defeated amendment and bill change nothing that needs enforcing; how far the 2025 protections are applied is in their share above.

rows.label: Texas: all adjustments
rows.explainer: The product of the Texas branch's adjustments.

rows.label: Florida and Oklahoma: charitable bailouts a year the 2025 bills threatened
rows.explainer: Five of the charity's 14 bail sites are in Florida (Jacksonville, Orlando, Pensacola) and Oklahoma (Oklahoma City, Tulsa): about a third of its roughly 3,300 bailouts a year, 1,000, plus local community bail funds there. 1,200 (500 to 2,500), our judgment.

rows.label: Share of those bailouts lost had the restrictions passed
rows.explainer: Georgia's SB 63 (2024) stopped the charity's bailouts there until a court's preliminary injunction; elsewhere funds would move their money to other states, where it frees others, after a lag. Our judgment: half the bailouts lost for the years counted (20% to 90%).

rows.label: Florida and Oklahoma: people a year kept out of detention
rows.explainer: Bailouts kept, times the shared share of the days clients would really have served.

rows.label: Days of detention avoided per bailout
rows.explainer: The charity's own 40 days per bailout (2025 report).

rows.label: Florida and Oklahoma: person-years of detention avoided a year
Florida and Oklahoma: years counted, discounted
rows.explainer: A blocked bill counts the site's years for a won reform; it takes effect at once (no wait).

rows.label: Florida and Oklahoma: share of the bills' defeat due to the opposition
rows.explainer: The bail bond industry's bills had sponsors in both legislatures; the charity says it 'decisively blocked' them. A share of an outcome already in: 40% (15% to 70%), our judgment.

rows.label: Florida and Oklahoma: the charity's share of the opposition's resources
rows.explainer: The charity was the bills' main target and led the opposition with local funds and defenders: 40% (20% to 70%).

rows.label: Florida and Oklahoma: evidence adjustment
rows.explainer: The bailouts and their days are the charity's own counts; the share lost is judged: 0.8 (0.5 to 1).

rows.label: Florida and Oklahoma: missing outcome data
rows.explainer: Thin: what the bills would have done is judged, so the site's discount for missing data applies.

rows.label: Florida and Oklahoma: share of bailed-out people who stay out until the case closes
rows.explainer: The charity's clients made 93% of their court dates (2024 report); some who miss one are held again. 0.93 (0.85 to 1), as in the bail model.

rows.label: Florida and Oklahoma: all adjustments
rows.explainer: The product of the charitable-bail branch's adjustments.

rows.label: Texas: income, public money and deaths a year of campaigning, in units of value, adjusted
rows.formula: (tx_people_per_year * ln_gain_per_release * $uov_per_ln_consumption + tx_detyears_per_year * 365 * @incarceration.jail_cost_per_day * public_uov_per_dollar + (tx_detyears_per_year + tx_people_per_year * sentence_years_per_release) * deaths_per_detention_year * value_per_death) * tx_discounted_years * tx_total_adj / campaign_years
rows.explainer: Released people's earnings, the counties' jail costs saved (the shared marginal cost of a day) and the deaths detention causes, over the years counted, adjusted, per year of campaigns.

rows.label: Florida and Oklahoma: WELLBYs a year of campaigning, adjusted

rows.explainer: Detention and sentence years avoided times the shared life-satisfaction loss, over the years counted, adjusted, per year of campaigns.

rows.label: Florida and Oklahoma: income, public money and deaths a year of campaigning, in units of value, adjusted
rows.formula: (cb_people_per_year * ln_gain_per_release * $uov_per_ln_consumption + cb_detyears_per_year * 365 * @incarceration.jail_cost_per_day * public_uov_per_dollar + (cb_detyears_per_year + cb_people_per_year * sentence_years_per_release) * deaths_per_detention_year * value_per_death) * cb_discounted_years * cb_total_adj / campaign_years
rows.explainer: Released people's earnings, the counties' jail costs saved (the shared marginal cost of a day) and the deaths detention causes, over the years counted, adjusted, per year of campaigns.

rows.label: Years a won reform counts

rows.explainer: The shared rate over the wait (none).

rows.label: Years counted, discounted (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.explainer: Each branch's discounted years, weighted by its detention avoided.

rows.label: People released by casework
rows.explainer: The bail itself is charityevals' separate bail model.

rows.label: Years each released person would have served
rows.explainer: No casework in this model.

rows.label: Life satisfaction per year released
rows.explainer: The shared figure.

rows.label: WELLBYs per person released, discounted
rows.explainer: The person's own years, discounted at the shared rate (a release isn't a won reform).

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.formula: (tx_detyears_per_year * tx_discounted_years * tx_total_adj * tx_evidence_adj + cb_detyears_per_year * cb_discounted_years * cb_total_adj * cb_evidence_adj) / (tx_detyears_per_year * tx_discounted_years * tx_total_adj + cb_detyears_per_year * cb_discounted_years * cb_total_adj)
rows.explainer: Each branch's own adjustment, weighted by its adjusted detention avoided.

rows.label: Counterfactual (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.formula: (tx_detyears_per_year * tx_discounted_years * tx_total_adj * tx_counterfactual_adj + cb_detyears_per_year * cb_discounted_years * cb_total_adj * cb_counterfactual_adj) / (tx_detyears_per_year * tx_discounted_years * tx_total_adj + cb_detyears_per_year * cb_discounted_years * cb_total_adj)
rows.explainer: Each branch's own adjustment, weighted by its adjusted detention avoided.

rows.label: The charity's share of resources (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.formula: (tx_detyears_per_year * tx_discounted_years * tx_total_adj * tx_attribution_share + cb_detyears_per_year * cb_discounted_years * cb_total_adj * cb_attribution_share) / (tx_detyears_per_year * tx_discounted_years * tx_total_adj + cb_detyears_per_year * cb_discounted_years * cb_total_adj)
rows.explainer: Each branch's own share, weighted by its adjusted detention avoided.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of resources, the outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only.

rows.label: Share of the wins delivered (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.formula: (tx_detyears_per_year * tx_discounted_years * tx_total_adj * tx_implementation_adj + cb_detyears_per_year * cb_discounted_years * cb_total_adj * cb_implementation_adj) / (tx_detyears_per_year * tx_discounted_years * tx_total_adj + cb_detyears_per_year * cb_discounted_years * cb_total_adj)
rows.explainer: Each branch's own implementation share, weighted by its adjusted detention avoided.

rows.label: Missing outcome data (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.formula: (tx_detyears_per_year * tx_discounted_years * tx_total_adj * tx_missing_data_adj + cb_detyears_per_year * cb_discounted_years * cb_total_adj * cb_missing_data_adj) / (tx_detyears_per_year * tx_discounted_years * tx_total_adj + cb_detyears_per_year * cb_discounted_years * cb_total_adj)
rows.explainer: Both branches are thin and take the site's discount for missing data in their own adjustments.

rows.label: All adjustments (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.formula: (tx_detyears_per_year * tx_discounted_years * tx_total_adj + cb_detyears_per_year * cb_discounted_years * cb_total_adj) / (tx_detyears_per_year * tx_discounted_years + cb_detyears_per_year * cb_discounted_years)
rows.explainer: Each branch's adjustments, weighted by its detention avoided.

rows.label: Side effect: backlash, as a share of the value
rows.explainer: Charitable bail's visibility helps the bail bond industry's campaigns against it (Georgia 2024, the 2025 bills); the campaigns the charity lost (Georgia's SB 63 in 2024) are already at zero value here. -3% (-15% to 0), our judgment.

rows.label: Side effect: children and partners spared a parent's detention, as a share of the value
rows.explainer: As in the bail model: a parent jailed for weeks or months costs children care and income; 10% (0 to 30%).

rows.label: Side effects, as a share of the value
rows.explainer: The two side effects above, each read through the side-effect weight.
